entry_requirement_note: Official eligibility page: "The right to enrol have: Applicants who have completed a professional or university undergraduate study programme in the field of technical, natural and social science and have obtained 180 or more ECTS credits"; also holders of sub-3-year higher vocational (cro. visa strucna sprema, VSS) qualifications with a title equivalent to baccalaureus. FIELD, NOT TOTAL, IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT: "Exceptionally, the right to enrol may be granted to applicants who have previously completed a study of an appropriate level that is not from the specified fields, with the mandatory completion of a preparatory programme"; and "Applicants who have not previously completed studies in the field of technical sciences, computer science or social sciences may be required to take a preparatory programme... as a rule, must do so before enrolling... The price of the preparatory programme is not included in the annual tuition fee but is charged additionally." No per-subject ECTS quantities are published - the preparatory obligation is decided by document review plus an interview that also assesses grades and English. No recency rule published. NOTE stručni/sveučilišni: this is a PROFESSIONAL graduate programme (title mag. ing. comp.), and professional as well as university undergraduate degrees are explicitly accepted.

Official eligibility page: "The right to enrol have: Applicants who have completed a professional or university undergraduate study programme in the field of social, natural or technical sciences and have obtained 180 or more ECTS credits"; also sub-3-year higher vocational (VSS) qualifications with a baccalaureus-equivalent title. Applicants from outside those fields may be admitted exceptionally with a mandatory preparatory programme; "Applicants who have not previously completed studies in the field of technical sciences, computer science or social sciences may be required to take a preparatory programme" (charged separately from tuition, normally completed before enrolment). No per-subject ECTS quantities published. No recency rule published.

Official eligibility page, "Formal Enrollment Requirements for the graduate programme": "Applicants must hold any three-year bachelor's degree equivalent to 180 ECTS credits." SUBJECT COMPOSITION RULE (directly relevant to a Business Intelligence licence): "If the degree is in the field of Economy, no further qualifications are required. If the degree is in any other field but the student has successfully completed at least a few basic economics courses, no further qualifications are required. If such basic economics courses have not been completed, we will prepare an individual preparatory program (typically a few additional FREE fully online courses in basic economics...)." No minimum ECTS is attached to the "basic economics courses" requirement - it is assessed by document review plus interview. Preparatory courses are free here and may be taken after enrolment/while awaiting a visa. No recency rule published.

No total prior-ECTS floor is published (a bachelor degree is required; holders of a foreign bachelor MUST undergo the credit recognition procedure). The binding constraint is SUBJECT CREDITS, from the official 2026 credit-recognition table ("honnan-hova tabla"): "The minimum number of credits required for admission to the Master's programme is 70 ECTS credits" in - Natural Sciences (Analysis, Probability Theory, Statistics, Operations Research, Mathematics, Informatics) 10 ECTS; - Business and Human Resource Management (Economics, Business Economics, Finance, Law, EU Studies, Management, Management and Decision Making) 20 ECTS; - Informatics (IT Architectures, Operational Systems, IT Networks, Programming Theory, Programming Languages, Programme Design, Database Handling, IR Architectures, Quality Assurance, Integrated Development Tools, Development Support, IT Audit, Integrated Business Management Systems, Special Applications) 40 ECTS. ADMISSION FLOOR: "To be admitted to the Master's programme, you must have at least 40 ECTS credits in the listed subject areas" (full requirement 70). Missing credits must be acquired during the MSc. Separate rule for a Computer Science Operational Engineering bachelor: at least 60 ECTS (Natural Sciences 10 / Business and HR Management 20 / Informatics 30), to be acquired within 2 active semesters after admission. No recency rule found. AMBIGUITY: a Business Intelligence licence from a business school is likely short on the 40 ECTS Informatics block - the transcript must be audited against the named informatics course list.

No total prior-ECTS floor published; bachelor degree required and the credit recognition procedure is MANDATORY for holders of a foreign bachelor degree. Official 2026 credit-recognition table: "The minimum number of credits required for admission to the Master's programme is 36 ECTS credits, acquired during previous studies or work experience... in the following areas: - Methodology (including courses in applied methods: Analysis, Linear Algebra, Probability, Statistics): 12 ECTS credits (maximum 6 ECTS credits of which can be acquired through catch up courses); - Programming skills (knowledge of any programming language, in particular Python or R): 12 ECTS credits (maximum 6 ECTS credits of which can be acquired through catch up courses); - Knowledge of economics (Business Economics, Accounting, Finance, Marketing, Management and Organization): 12 ECTS credits (12 ECTS credits of which can be acquired through catch up courses). To be admitted to the Master's programme, applicants must have 24 ECTS credits in the listed subject areas." So 24 ECTS is the hard entry floor, 36 ECTS the full requirement; at most 6+6+12 = 24 may be made up by catch-up courses. Admission also involves an in-house written examination. This programme does not appear in the 2025 version of the table (new for September 2026 intake). No recency rule found.

No total prior-ECTS floor published; bachelor degree required, credit recognition procedure MANDATORY for a foreign bachelor. Official 2026 credit-recognition table (identical wording in the 2025 table): "The minimum number of credits required for admission to the Master's programme is 36 ECTS credits... - Methodology (including courses in applied methods: Analysis, Linear Algebra, Matrix Algebra, Probability, Statistics): 12 ECTS credits (cannot be acquired through catch up courses); - Programming skills (knowledge of any programming language, in particular Python or R): 12 ECTS credits (cannot be acquired through catch up courses); - Knowledge of economics or social sciences (Economics, Sociology, Political Science): 12 ECTS credits (6 ECTS credits of which can be acquired through catch up courses). To be admitted to the Master's programme, applicants must have 30 ECTS credits in the listed subject areas." HARD BLOCK: the 12 ECTS Methodology and 12 ECTS Programming credits CANNOT be made up by catch-up courses - they must already be on the transcript. The 2025 table states the same split as 12/12/6 = 30 ECTS at entry. No recency rule found.

No prior-ECTS floor is published. UTM International admission rules require, for 2nd-cycle (master's) enrolment, only "the copy and legalized translation of the bachelor's degree and the supplement to the degree or the equivalents of these documents" (apostilled/supra-legalised, translated), plus a 100 EUR admission fee and a Ministry of Education and Research confirmation of study entitlement. SUBJECT PREREQUISITES (programme page, no ECTS attached): "for candidates from the same field: completion of the minimum curriculum indicated in the study plan. The minimum curriculum is specified for candidates from the same domain of study (Computer Science, Information Technology, or related domains) and includes foundational courses: Numerical Methods, Data Structures and Algorithms, Object Oriented Programming, Procedural Programming, Interactive programming (Python), Human-computer interaction (HCI); for candidates from different fields: Candidates must complete the required prerequisites before admission or during the program through designated bridging modules." Programme is 2 years / 120 ECTS, 3 000 EUR per year. English proficiency required (exempt with a C1 certificate or an English-taught degree). ANACEC accreditation status for this Data Science programme is NOT stated on either the UTM International programme page or the FCIM programme page - still unconfirmed. No recency rule published.

institution: Academy of Performing Arts in Prague - Film and TV School (FAMU)
entry_requirement_note: No credit/ECTS floor published. FAMU General admission requirements for master's study 2027/28: open to applicants "who have completed their bachelor's degree studies or are in the last year of their bachelor's degree studies", with "a copy of your Bachelor's Degree diploma"; "to enrol in September you need to undergo the diploma recognition procedure" (Czech nostrification of the foreign degree) - this is the practical gate for a Tunisian licence, not a credit count. Department page states no field requirement: "applicants who have not studied photography under a bachelor's degree programme may also apply", only "previous experience in the creative use of photography and technical images" is expected. Selection is a two-round talent exam (portfolio + motivation letter, then conceptual assignment and interview by video call). Standard length 2 years (Photography). No recency rule published.

institution: Academy of Performing Arts in Prague - Film and TV School (FAMU)
entry_requirement_note: No credit/ECTS floor published. Department "How to apply" page requires applicants to have "completed a Bachelor's Degree in film or a related field" - a FIELD restriction, not a credit one - plus English at B2 (CEFR). Application materials: passport scan, teacher's letter of recommendation, structured CV, motivation letter (max 1000 words), application fee (CZK 967), scan of the bachelor's diploma (English or translated), a short film (max 40 min), written film analysis (600-1200 words), photographic storyboard (max 17 shots), audiovisual self-portrait (max 1 min). Two rounds: materials assessment then MS Teams interview. FAMU general rules add the mandatory foreign-diploma recognition procedure before September enrolment. Standard length 3 years. No recency rule published.

institution: Academy of Performing Arts in Prague - Film and TV School (FAMU)
entry_requirement_note: No credit/ECTS floor published. Cinematography Department (CIN KK) entry-requirements document: applicants must have "A successful completion of a Bachelor's degree at a college with a similar or related focus, possibly accompanied by practical experience with filmmaking" - a field restriction. Non-credit subject prerequisites are listed: "Knowledge in maths: general secondary school level; particularly simple equations, goniometric functions, common logarithm. Knowledge in physics: general secondary school level; particularly electromagnetic radiation, optics. International cinematography and the cameraman's job. General knowledge in the field of art." Own still camera with interchangeable lenses required; English B2 minimum; two-stage entrance exam, interviews by Zoom in February; application deadline 21 January 2027 for 2027/28; fee CZK 2 111. FAMU general rules add the mandatory foreign-diploma recognition procedure before September enrolment. CAUTION: the departmental entry-requirements PDF is dated November 2019 (its deadlines are stale) though the degree requirement is unchanged on the current How-to-apply page. Standard length 3 years.

institution: Academy of Performing Arts in Prague - Film and TV School (FAMU)
entry_requirement_note: No credit/ECTS floor published and no field restriction: the programme is described as "a three-year follow-up Master's program for graduate students who already received a BA degree in Cinema or another field". English at B2 (CEFR) minimum. Selection is by talent test: round one, five committee members assess submitted materials (knowledge of the craft of filmmaking, ability to develop dramatic character and plot, ability to convey story audiovisually); round two by video call. Application window for 2027/28: 2 November 2026 to 21 January 2027. FAMU general admission requirements 2027/28 add: bachelor completed (or final year) plus the foreign-diploma recognition procedure required to enrol in September. No recency rule published.

No prior-ECTS floor published. EKA MA admissions: "The requirement for admission to master level studies is a bachelor's degree, higher education obtained on the basis of professional higher education curriculum, or other relevant qualification that gives access to master level studies in Estonia." No field restriction for Animation beyond "Must hold a bachelor's degree" plus English at B2. GRADE FLOOR (behaves like a hard cutoff): "Applicants need to have a bachelor's degree or its equivalent, and at least 60% of the highest possible CGPA to be eligible to apply to our master's degree programmes." Foreign qualifications are recognised "on the basis of assessments and opinions of the Estonian ENIC/NARIC Centre". Tunisia is NOT listed on EKA's country-specific requirements page (only Nigeria, Ghana, Cameroon, Gambia, Liberia, Ethiopia, Sierra Leone, Australia, Bangladesh, Canada, China, France, Hong Kong, India, Iran, Iraq, Pakistan, USA) - unlisted countries must contact admissions@artun.ee, so document requirements for a Tunisian licence are unresolved. Application fee EUR 80. No recency rule published.

No prior-ECTS floor published. Same institution-wide rule as all EKA MA programmes: "The requirement for admission to master level studies is a bachelor's degree, higher education obtained on the basis of professional higher education curriculum, or other relevant qualification that gives access to master level studies in Estonia", with foreign qualifications assessed by the Estonian ENIC/NARIC Centre. GRADE FLOOR: "at least 60% of the highest possible CGPA to be eligible to apply to our master's degree programmes". No prior-field or subject-credit requirement is published; selection is on portfolio/motivation and interview. Tunisia is not covered by EKA's country-specific requirements page - contact admissions@artun.ee. Application fee EUR 80. No recency rule published.

No prior-ECTS floor published. Tallinn University "Requirements and Procedure for the Admission to Degree Studies": candidates for master's studies must "have been awarded a Bachelor's degree or a corresponding qualification" and meet programme-specific requirements; the university may send documents to the Estonian ENIC/NARIC Centre for qualification assessment. GRADE FLOOR: "at least 60% of the possible maximum results" is expected. Programme page requires "Completed Bachelor's degree or the equivalent"; no prior field is required, though "previous study or work experience in the fields of film, media, or art" is sought. Entrance exam out of 100: CV and creative portfolio 35%, interview 20%, creative assignment 35%, additional interview 10%; 80+ guarantees admission, 70-79 ranked competitively, minimum 60 over the first three rounds to reach the additional interview. Own camera needed for the creative task. No recency rule published.

No prior-ECTS floor published. Institution-wide rule: master's candidates must "have been awarded a Bachelor's degree or a corresponding qualification" and meet programme-specific requirements, with foreign qualifications assessable via the Estonian ENIC/NARIC Centre; GRADE FLOOR of "at least 60% of the possible maximum results". Programme page requires only a "Completed Bachelor's degree" with no restriction on the field of prior study and no subject-credit prerequisites. Entrance exam: motivation letter 50% and online (Zoom) interview 50%, each scored out of 50; minimum 70 points combined required for admission. Proof of English proficiency required. No recency rule published.

No total prior-ECTS floor published; bachelor degree required and the credit recognition procedure is MANDATORY for holders of a foreign bachelor degree. Official 2026 credit-recognition table (unchanged from 2025): credits required for entry 30 ECTS, minimum credits required for entry 30 ECTS - i.e. the full and minimum requirements coincide, so there is NO catch-up allowance. "To be admitted to the Master's programme, you must have at least 30 ECTS credits in the listed subject areas. Business and Management, Network Communication, Human Resources, Cultural Anthropology, Science of Culture, Communication, Marketing, Media Theory, Media Culture, Media Literacy, Work Psychology, Foundations of Interculture, Arts and Arts Communication, Linguistics, International Communication, Special Media Literacy, Sociology, Social Psychology, PR." AMBIGUITY: the 30 ECTS is a single pooled figure across that subject list with no per-category split published. No recency rule found.

institution: Moholy-Nagy University of Art and Design (MOME)
entry_requirement_note: No prior-ECTS floor and no subject-credit table published (unlike Corvinus, MOME publishes no credit-recognition credit categories for its English-language MAs). Official requirement: "A university degree (bachelor's degree/college degree or master's degree) is a precondition for applying to our masters' programmes. Please note that foreign degrees must be accredited and equivalent to a Hungarian bachelor's degree." Those graduating in the current year must supply an official letter confirming graduation. Language: B2 English (higher preferred). Selection: professional portfolio reviewed by a committee of professors, then an admission interview (online for international applicants) assessing professional preparedness, creative vision and general/cultural knowledge. Portfolio max 500 MB, must demonstrate prior experience and artistic skills relevant to animation. No recency rule published. AMBIGUITY: "accredited and equivalent to a Hungarian bachelor's degree" is the only lever by which a 3-year 180 ECTS licence could be questioned; no duration or credit threshold is stated.

institution: Moholy-Nagy University of Art and Design (MOME)
entry_requirement_note: No prior-ECTS floor and no subject-credit table published. Official requirement is identical across MOME's English MAs: "A university degree (bachelor's degree/college degree or master's degree) is a precondition for applying to our masters' programmes. Please note that foreign degrees must be accredited and equivalent to a Hungarian bachelor's degree." B2 English minimum. Selection by portfolio plus interview; the portfolio should contain case studies of digital product work (apps, websites), and school, fictional or redesign projects are explicitly acceptable, with no minimum page count (10-50 recommended). MOME materials list animation, media design, photography, design, object creation, design graphics, textile design, architecture and design culture as relevant bachelor backgrounds, but the published precondition is any university degree. No recency rule published.

institution: Moholy-Nagy University of Art and Design (MOME)
entry_requirement_note: No prior-ECTS floor and no subject-credit table published. Official requirement: "A university degree (bachelor's degree/college degree or master's degree) is a precondition for applying to our masters' programmes. Please note that foreign degrees must be accredited and equivalent to a Hungarian bachelor's degree." B2 English minimum. Selection by portfolio (photographic work, ideally 3-4 projects or 20-30 photographs, photo book designs, installation documentation, each with a short description) reviewed by a committee, followed by an admission interview, held online for international applicants. No prior field of study is required and no recency rule is published.

programme_name_exact: Graphic Design and Multimedia Art (second-cycle, full-time, English-language)
entry_requirement_note: No prior-ECTS floor published. Official admission rules: "Candidates for full-time second-cycle studies must hold a Master's or Bachelor's degree (a degree in arts is not required)" - explicitly no field restriction, though "candidates may need to supplement individual subjects or complete additional coursework if their bachelor's degree lacks required knowledge" (no ECTS quantities attached). Selection is by portfolio (single PDF, max 25 MB, min 100 DPI, each work with title, year, description and technique, submitted three business days before the interview) plus an interview at which the candidate presents the proposed master's project concept; no written entrance exam. English B2 certificate required. NON-EU DOCUMENT GATE relevant to a Tunisian licence: a written decision of the NAWA Director confirming eligibility to continue studies is required for diplomas issued outside the EU/EFTA/OECD/Ukraine/China, and apostille/legalisation is required (Tunisia is not on the exemption list). Programme is 3 semesters full-time. No recency rule published.
